plan.title: Treated vs control DE with confounded batch (transparent report)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context is explicit: 12000 genes x 13 columns (12 samples + gene column), 6 treated vs 6 control, raw salmon counts, and batch B1/B2 is perfectly confounded with condition (all controls in B1, all treated in B2). This is a structural design flaw, not a data-quality issue: no computational method (ComBat, limma removeBatchEffect, RUVSeq, SVA, or including batch as a covariate in a GLM) can separate a treatment effect from a batch effect when every sample of one condition sits in one batch and every sample of the other condition sits in the other. Any model with both terms is rank-deficient (batch and condition are the same design column up to relabeling), and any correction method that estimates and removes 'batch' will simultaneously and unavoidably remove all or part of the true condition signal, because they are mathematically identical partitions of the 12 samples. This has been formally documented as an unrecoverable design defect (Leek et al. 2010, Nat Rev Genet, PMID 20838408 — batch effects correlated with the outcome of interest lead to incorrect conclusions and cannot be reliably corrected post hoc). The only honest path forward is: (1) run standard QC to confirm the confound is real and not an artifact of the metadata, (2) run the DE analysis as specified, clearly flagging that any resulting gene list reflects 'treated vs control OR B2 vs B1' with no way to attribute the source, (3) explicitly quantify how much of the observed differential signal could plausibly be batch-driven using structure that does not depend on the confounded label (e.g., PCA/clustering to see if batch and condition co-vary with the same drivers, and technical-covariate proxies like library size, GC content, if derivable from counts) so the report can characterize confidence rather than assert causality, and (4) produce a report that states the confound prominently, marks the DE result as uninterpretable with respect to treatment causation, and recommends a follow-up experiment with balanced batches before any biological claims are made. No enrichment, druggability, or mechanistic interpretation step is included, because building interpretation on top of a gene list that cannot be attributed to treatment vs batch would fabricate confidence the data does not support.
